I am a 33-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with eight years in the fields and a middle school education. My family has seven people, and with some of us working off-farm in nearby towns or factories, I cannot be in the fields every single day. My 4.1 mu is not much land, so I have to be practical and avoid risky bets. I rely on the wheat-maize rotation on 3.1 mu because it gives me grain for food and feed plus two harvests a year. The remaining 1 mu I plant with cotton for cash income, though it is labor-intensive and needs more watching.

It is early spring now, and my winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I will irrigate three times using my well—at green-up, jointing, and grain filling—because water is the key to yield here. Fertilizer prices have been high, so I will not overdo it: about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, split as topdressing, plus phosphorus and potassium. I will spray pesticide twice, once for weeds and once for insects if they show up. I rotary-tilled the plot last autumn, so I only need light harrowing now. I expect around 480 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After the wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize on the same 3.1 mu using no-tillage direct seeding. There is only a short window between wheat harvest and maize planting, and no-tillage saves me diesel, labor, and soil moisture. Maize needs less hand labor, which is good because my family is busy with off-farm work then. I will irrigate twice—at the jointing-tasseling stage and during grain filling—and apply nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Two pesticide applications should be enough. I expect about 580 kg per mu.

For cotton, I will rotary-till the 1 mu plot in spring and plant an improved variety. Cotton needs more care: three irrigations, more potassium than the grains, and four pesticide sprays to control bollworms and aphids. My wife and parents can help with pest scouting and picking. I expect about 90 kg of seed cotton per mu. I will not chase maximum yields with costly inputs; I aim for stable, decent returns that feed my family and leave some cash in hand.
